'''Thavamani Jegajothivel Pandian''' (born 15 June 1939), a retired professor of [[Madurai Kamaraj University]] (MKU), is an Indian geneticist and ecologist, known for his pioneering studies in [[bioenergetics]] and [[animal ecology]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=226 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=28 September 2016}}</ref> A recipient of the [[WorldFish]] Naga Award, he is a former chairman of the ''Task Force Committee on Aqua and Marine Biotechnology'' of the [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India,<ref name="List of Members Task Force Committee">{{cite web | url=http://www.dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/List-of-Members-Task-Force-Committee.pdf | title=List of Members Task Force Committee | publisher=Department of Biotechnology | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> a former president and a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] and an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]].<ref name="T J Pandian on National Institute of Oceanography">{{cite web | url=http://www.nio.org/nio/uploadevents/195_0_Prof_Pandian_Lecture_Abst.pdf | title=T J Pandian on National Institute of Oceanography | publisher=National Institute of Oceanography | work=Scientist profile | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1984, for his contributions to biological sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=19 September 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Chennai Presidency College Main.jpg|thumb|235px|[[Presidency College, Chennai]].]]
Thavamani Jegajothivel Pandian, born on 15 June 1939 in [[Palamedu]], a small town in [[Madurai district]] of the [[South India]]n state of [[Tamil Nadu]] to Kumarasamy Thavamani and Valliammal couple, graduated in science from [[Thiagarajar College]], [[Madurai]] in 1960 and completed his master's degree from [[Presidency College, Chennai]] in 1962, both the colleges affiliated to [[Madras University]], before securing a doctoral degree (PhD) in 1965 from the same university.<ref name="Fellow profile - National Academy of Agricultural Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://naasindia.org/detail.php?id=329 | title=Fellow profile - National Academy of Agricultural Sciences | publisher=National Academy of Agricultural Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> His post-doctoral studies were at Bilogische Anstalt, Helgoland, Germany and he obtained the degree of Doctor of Natural Sciences ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) from [[Kiel University]] in 1968. Returning to India, he started his career at [[Bangalore University]] as a lecturer in 1968 and moved to his home town in 1971 to join [[Madurai Kamaraj University]] as a reader where he served till his superannuation, holding positions of a professor (1976–92) and a senior professor (1994–95).<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N87-0972 | title=Indian Fellow - Pandian | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> In between, he served as a visiting scientist at [[Oxford University]] (1973), as a visiting professor at [[Columbia University]] and [[University of South Carolina]] (1981–82), as an overseas associate at [[Kyoto University]] (1989) and as a UNESCO lecturer at [[Ghent University]] (2003–04). Post his superannuation, he held the position of a National Professor of the [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]] from 1996 to 2002, an Emeritus Scientist of the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] from 2002 to 2005 and an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] senior scientist from 2005 to 2009.{{Refn|group=note|Based at [[Annamalai University]]}} He has chaired the ''Task Force Committee on Aqua and Marine Biotechnology'' of the [[Department of Biotechnology]]<ref name="List of Members Task Force Committee" /> and is associated with Ecology Institute, Germany as a visiting scientist since 1985 and with [[MS Swaminathan Research Foundation]] as a visiting professor since 1996.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" /> He also served the councils of the Indian National Science Academy in 1990 and National Academy of Agricultural Sciences from 1998 to 2000.<ref name="Fellow profile - National Academy of Agricultural Sciences" />

Pandian is married to Muthu Shanthakumari and the couple has a son, Sathish Kinne Pandian who is a urologist.<ref name="Sathish Kinne Pandian">{{cite web | url=http://www.mciindia.org/ViewDetails.aspx?ID=338973 | title=Sathish Kinne Pandian | publisher=Medical Council of India | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> The family lives in Madurai.<ref name="Fellow profile - National Academy of Agricultural Sciences" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:Ameiurus melas by Duane Raver.png|thumb|left|A species of catfish ([[Ameiurus melas]])]]
Pandian's early work was in the field of [[bioenergetics]] and focusing on metabolism, he developed a model for predicting the transformation of food energy into growth.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=28 September 2016 | pages=33}}</ref> He published his research findings in ''Marine Biology'' journal of [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] in an article, ''Intake, digestion, absorption and conversion of food in the fishes Megalops cyprinoides and Ophiocephalus striatus'', which eventually became a citation classic.<ref name="Intake, digestion, absorption and conversion of food in the fishes Megalops cyprinoides and Ophiocephalus striatus">{{cite journal | url=https://garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1983/A1983RK20200001.pdf | title=Intake, digestion, absorption and conversion of food in the fishes Megalops cyprinoides and Ophiocephalus striatus | author=Pandian T. J. | journal=Marine Biology | date=October 1983 | volume=1 | pages=16–32 | doi=10.1007/bf00346690| s2cid=83957482 }}</ref> Subsequently, shifting his attention to the sexuality of fish, he demonstrated that the sperm survived in [[catfish]] for over 240 days if they were preserved at -20<sup>o</sup> degree Celsius and could still be fertilized, a discovery which had commercial relevance in places where [[liquid nitrogen]] is not easily available.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" /> Later, he created the first [[transgenic]] fish from preserved sperm and genome-inactivated eggs of compatible species which helped him to generate ''interspecific and intergeneric [[androgenetic]] clones''. Furthering the researches, he created ''supermales'' (with YY chromosomes) of [[tilapia]], [[Barb (fish)|barbs]] and [[guppy|guppies]] (Poecilia reticulata) and ''superfemales'' (ZZ) in molly ([[Poecilia sphenops]]) species, reportedly for the first time in India.<ref name="T J Pandian on National Institute of Oceanography" /> He used these monosex organisms to mass-produce monosex progenies in catfish. He is also credited with the cloning and production of fish-based ''[[growth hormone]] gene transformation [[Vector (molecular biology)|vectors]]''<ref name="Year Book entry - NIIST">{{cite web | url=http://www.niist.res.in/english/wp-content/files/SampleYearBookEntry.pdf | title=Year Book entry - NIIST | publisher=National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016 | archive-date=16 January 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116160112/http://www.niist.res.in/english/wp-content/files/SampleYearBookEntry.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> and with the restoration of [[rosy barb]] species using preserved sperms and genome-inactivated eggs of [[tiger barb]].<ref name="T J Pandian on National Institute of Oceanography" /> His researches are documented in a number of books which include ''Animal Energetics: Bivalvia through reptilia'',<ref name="Pandian1987">{{cite book|author=T. J. Pandian|title=Animal Energetics: Bivalvia through reptilia|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3GIXAQAAIAAJ|year=1987|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-544792-8}}</ref> ''Animal Energetics: Protozoa through insecta'',<ref name="PandianVernberg1987">{{cite book|author1=T. J. Pandian|author2=F. John Vernberg|title=Animal Energetics: Protozoa through insecta|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UpjwAAAAMAAJ|year=1987|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-544791-1}}</ref> ''Sex Determination in Fish'',<ref name="Pandian2011">{{cite book|author=T. J. Pandian|title=Sex Determination in Fish|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eAjSBQAAQBAJ|date=2 September 2011|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4398-7919-1}}</ref> ''Genetic Sex Differentiation in Fish'',<ref name="Pandian2012">{{cite book|author=T. J. Pandian|title=Genetic Sex Differentiation in Fish|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9EZvJQwsJBgC|date=5 June 2012|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-57808-799-0}}</ref> ''Environmental Sex Differentiation in Fish''<ref name="Pandian2014">{{cite book|author=T. J. Pandian|title=Environmental Sex Differentiation in Fish|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EtfMBQAAQBAJ|date=22 December 2014|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4822-5438-9}}</ref> and ''Reproduction and Development in Crustacea'',<ref name="Pandian2016">{{cite book|author=T. J. Pandian|title=Reproduction and Development in Crustacea|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LML1CwAAQBAJ|date=5 April 2016|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4987-4829-2}}</ref> and over 250 science articles; [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific papers, has listed 133 of them.<ref name="T. J. Pandian on ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/researcher/50358788_Thavamani_Jegajothivel_Pandian | title=T. J. Pandian on ResearchGate | work=Author profile | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref>

Pandian was one among the biologists who founded the Asian Fisheries Society (AFS), a non-profit scientific society for the promotion of fisheries and aquaculture, in 1984 and sat in its fourth council from 1992 to 1995.<ref name="Fourth Council (1992-1995)">{{cite web | url=http://www.asianfisheriessociety.org/council.php?id=23 | title=Fourth Council (1992-1995) | publisher=Asian Fisheries Society | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> He is a former member of the governing body of the [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]] and the academic councils of the [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] and the [[Central Institute of Fisheries Education]].<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" /> He has been associated with several science journals including ''Journal of Asian Fisheries Science'', [[Hydrobiologia]], [[Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology]], [[Marine Ecology Progress Series]], ''Indian Journal of Marine Sciences'' and ''Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research'' and is a former associate editor of [[Current Science]], consultant editor of ''Korean Journal of Aquaculture'' and a guest editor of Current Science and Hydrobiologia. He coordinated the USERS Project of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] during 2012–14<ref name="Fellow profile - National Academy of Agricultural Sciences" /> and has mentored 36 scholars in their doctoral researches.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" /> He is also a Member of the Governing Council and an Advisor of the ''Centre for Scientific & Applied Research'' of PSN College of Engineering and Technology, [[Tirunelveli]]<ref name="Mentors and Resource Persons">{{cite web | url=http://www.psnresearch.ac.in| title=Mentors and Resource Persons | publisher=PSN College of Engineering and Technology, Tirunelveli | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> and the ''Inspire Internship Camp'' of Velammal Institute of Technology, Panchetti<ref name="Inspire Internship Camp">{{cite web | url=http://www.velammalitech.edu.in/pdf/INSPIRE_2015_Mentors.pdf | title=Inspire Internship Camp | publisher=Velammal Institute of Technology | date=2015 | access-date=1 October 2016 | archive-date=26 January 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126114055/http://www.velammalitech.edu.in/pdf/INSPIRE_2015_Mentors.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="‘Inspire’ science camp from Monday">{{cite news | url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/inspire-science-camp-from-monday/article6346033.ece | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210615024109/https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/inspire-science-camp-from-monday/article6346033.ece | url-status=live | archive-date=15 June 2021 | title='Inspire' science camp from Monday | work=The Hindu | date=24 August 2014 | url-access=subscription | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> and he has attended several seminars and conferences to deliver keynote addresses,<ref name="Guest Lecture-Cancer Genetics - Role of the Laboratory">{{cite web | url=http://www.drngpasc.ac.in/clinical/activities.php | title=Guest Lecture-Cancer Genetics - Role of the Laboratory | publisher=Dr.N.G.P. Arts and Science College | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016 | archive-date=25 March 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170325115848/http://www.drngpasc.ac.in/clinical/activities.php | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Frontier Lecture">{{cite web | url=http://universityofcalicut.info/news/frontier_lect_dept_zoology.pdf | title=Frontier Lecture | publisher=University of Calicut | date=March 2014 | access-date=1 October 2016 | archive-date=26 January 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126113913/http://universityofcalicut.info/news/frontier_lect_dept_zoology.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> notably the National Seminar on Sustainability of Seafood Production in 2006<ref name="National Seminar on Sustainability of Seafood Production">{{cite web | url=http://www.nio.org/index/option/com_eventdisplay/task/view/tid/4/sid/114/eid/39 | title=National Seminar on Sustainability of Seafood Production | publisher=National Institute of Oceanography | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> and the CSIR Foundation Day lecture in 2012.<ref name="CSIR Foundation Day lecture">{{cite web | url=http://www.nio.org/index/option/com_eventdisplay/task/view/tid/4/sid/24/eid/195 | title=CSIR Foundation Day lecture | publisher=National Institute of Oceanography | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Pandian, who held the National Lectureship and the National Fellowship of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] during 1985–86 and 1989–91 respectively, received the Hooker Award of the [[Indian Agricultural Research Institute]] in 1978.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" /> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1984 for his contributions to bioenergetics and animal ecology.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee" /> The next year, he received the ECI Prize of the Ecology Institute where he has been serving as an adviser since then.<ref name="ECI Prize ">{{cite web | url=https://www.int-res.com/ecology-institute/staff/ | title=ECI Prize | publisher=Ecology Institute | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> [[WorldFish]] awarded him the Naga Award in 1991 and three years later, he received the 1994 K.N. Bahl Memorial Gold Medal of the Society of Biosciences, Delhi.<ref name="Year Book entry - NIIST" /> The [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]] selected him as National Professor in 1996{{Refn|group=note|ICAR National Professorship was from 1996 to 2002}} and the Council for Science and Technology of the Government of Tamil Nadu chose him for the Tamil Nadu Scientist Award in 1997.<ref name="Indian Fellow - Pandian" />

Pandian is an elected fellow of a number of major Indian science academies. The [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected him as a fellow in 1984<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web | url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=P | title=NASI fellows | publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016 | archive-date=4 March 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304044529/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=P | url-status=dead }}</ref> and he became a fellow of the Indian Academy of Sciences, the next year.<ref name="Fellow Profile IAS">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Pandian,_Prof._Thavamani_Jegajothivel | title=Fellow Profile IAS | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> Two years later, he was elected as a fellow of the Indian National Science Academy, which was followed by his election as fellow by the [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]] in 1992. In 1999, he received the fellowship of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="T J Pandian - TWAS fellow">{{cite web | url=http://twas.org/member/pandian-thavamani-jegajothivel | title=T J Pandian - TWAS fellow | publisher=The World Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref>
